topics.title: Rotation and revolution of the Earth

learn.hook: Right now you are spinning with the Earth and also racing around the Sun, yet you feel perfectly still!
points: The Earth spins on its axis, an imaginary line through the North and South Poles. This spinning is called rotation.
The Earth rotates from west to east, once in about 24 hours. Rotation causes day and night, and makes the Sun appear to rise in the east and set in the west.
The Earth also moves around the Sun in a fixed path called its orbit. This is revolution, and one revolution takes about 365¼ days, which is one year.
The extra quarter days add up, so usually every fourth year has an extra day, 29 February. Such a year has 366 days and is called a leap year.
The Earth's axis is tilted. This tilt, along with revolution, gives us seasons. The Indian astronomer Aryabhata, about 1,500 years ago, wrote that the Earth rotates on its axis.

example.q: Why does the Sun appear to rise in the east every morning?
steps: The Earth rotates from west to east.
So places on the Earth turn towards the Sun from the eastern side first.
To us standing on the ground, the Sun seems to come up from the east.
example.answer: Because the Earth rotates from west to east, the Sun appears to rise in the east.

learn.reallife: When it is morning in India, it is evening or night in the USA, because only half of the rotating Earth faces the Sun at a time.

quiz.q: What is the rotation of the Earth?
quiz.explain: Rotation is the Earth turning on its axis. Moving around the Sun is revolution.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up rotation and revolution

quiz.q: About how many hours does the Earth take to rotate once?
quiz.explain: One rotation takes about 24 hours, which gives us one day and one night.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one rotation gives only daytime

quiz.q: What is caused by the rotation of the Earth?
quiz.explain: As the Earth spins, the side facing the Sun has day and the other side has night.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the effects of rotation and revolution

quiz.q: How many days are there in a leap year?
quiz.explain: A leap year has an extra day, 29 February, so it has 366 days.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the extra day

quiz.q: 2024 was a leap year. Which of these will be the next leap year?
quiz.explain: Leap years usually come every 4 years: 2024 + 4 = 2028.
quiz.mistake: Thinks leap years come every year or every 2 years

quiz.q: In which direction does the Earth rotate?
quiz.explain: The Earth turns from west to east. That is why the Sun, Moon and stars seem to move from east to west across the sky.
quiz.mistake: Takes the Sun's apparent motion as the Earth's real motion

quiz.q: What is one revolution of the Earth around the Sun?
quiz.explain: The Earth takes about 365 and a quarter days to go once around the Sun.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the time for rotation, the Moon's cycle and revolution

quiz.q: Which ancient Indian astronomer wrote that the Earth rotates on its axis?
quiz.explain: Aryabhata, about 1,500 years ago, explained the daily motion of the sky by the Earth's rotation.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up scientists from different fields and times

teach.ask: Gappu sees the Sun rise every morning and thinks the Sun is going around the Earth. What is really happening?
teach.praise: Tweet! The Earth spins to make day and night, and travels around the Sun to make a year. Gappu is spinning with joy!
teach.nudge: What does the Earth's spinning on its axis cause?

learn.hook: Diwali is celebrated on a moonless night (amavasya), while many festivals fall on full moon nights (purnima). The Moon has been India's calendar for ages!
points: The Moon does not make its own light. It shines because it reflects sunlight.
Half of the Moon is always lit by the Sun. As the Moon goes around the Earth, we see different amounts of this lit half. These shapes are the phases of the Moon.
New moon (amavasya): the lit half faces away from us, so we cannot see the Moon. Full moon (purnima): we see the whole lit half as a bright disc.
After the new moon the visible part grows (waxing, called Shukla Paksha); after the full moon it shrinks (waning, called Krishna Paksha).
One full cycle of phases takes about 29½ days. The same side of the Moon always faces the Earth.

example.q: Why can't we see the Moon on a new moon night even though it is in the sky?
steps: The Moon shines only by reflecting sunlight.
On new moon day the Moon is between the Earth and the Sun.
Its lit side faces the Sun, and its dark side faces us.
example.answer: Because the side of the Moon facing us is not lit by the Sun.

learn.reallife: Many Indian calendars and festivals follow the phases of the Moon, and fishermen watch the Moon because tides are stronger near new moon and full moon.

games.title: Moon facts
items: The Moon makes its own light.
The Moon reflects sunlight; it has no light of its own.
Half of the Moon is always lit by the Sun.
The half facing the Sun is always lit; we see different parts of it.
The waxing phase comes after the new moon.
After new moon, the bright part grows night by night until full moon.
The same side of the Moon always faces the Earth.
The Moon spins once in the same time it takes to go around the Earth.
Phases happen because the Earth's shadow covers the Moon every night.
Phases are due to how much of the Moon's lit half we can see. The Earth's shadow causes lunar eclipses, not phases.

quiz.q: Why does the Moon shine?
options: It reflects light from Earth's cities only
quiz.explain: The Moon is like a giant mirror-ball lit by the Sun; it has no light of its own.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Moon is a source of light

quiz.q: On which night is the Moon not visible?
quiz.explain: On new moon, the Moon's lit side faces away from us.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up new moon and full moon

quiz.q: When the Moon's visible part grows each night, the Moon is said to be:
quiz.explain: Waxing means growing. It happens from new moon to full moon (Shukla Paksha).
quiz.mistake: Mixes up waxing and waning

quiz.q: About how many days does the Moon take to go through all its phases once?
quiz.explain: One cycle of phases, from one new moon to the next, takes about 29 and a half days, roughly a month.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the Moon's cycle with a week or a year

quiz.q: Why do we see phases of the Moon?
options: The Earth's shadow covers it every night
We see different amounts of its sunlit half as it goes around the Earth
quiz.explain: The Moon is always round and half lit. Its position around the Earth changes how much of the lit half faces us.
quiz.mistake: Believes the Earth's shadow causes the phases

quiz.q: The period of the waning Moon, from full moon to new moon, is called:
quiz.explain: Shukla Paksha is the bright (waxing) half; Krishna Paksha is the dark (waning) half.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the two halves of the lunar month

quiz.q: Why do we always see the same face of the Moon from the Earth?
options: The Moon does not spin at all
The Moon spins once in the same time it takes to go around the Earth
The other side has no surface
quiz.explain: Because both take the same time, the same side keeps facing the Earth.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Moon does not rotate at all

quiz.q: A few days after the full moon, how will the Moon look?
options: A thin crescent that is growing
quiz.explain: After full moon, the bright part shrinks night by night, so the Moon starts to wane.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the order of the phases

teach.ask: Gappu sees the Moon as a thin smile one week and a big round plate another week. Does the Moon really change shape?
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! The Moon stays round; we just see more or less of its sunlit half. Gappu loves moon-watching!
teach.nudge: Where does the Moon's light come from?

learn.hook: Imagine the Sun going dark in the middle of the day! A total solar eclipse makes birds settle as if it were dusk, but it lasts only a few minutes.
points: An eclipse happens when the Sun, Earth and Moon come in a straight line and one casts a shadow on the other.
Solar eclipse: the Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth, and the Moon's shadow falls on the Earth. It can happen only on a new moon day.
Lunar eclipse: the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon, and the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon. It can happen only on a full moon night. In a total lunar eclipse the Moon often looks reddish.
Eclipses do not happen every month, because the Moon's path is slightly tilted compared to the Earth's path, so the three usually do not line up exactly.
Safety: never look at the Sun directly, even during a solar eclipse. Use proper certified solar eclipse glasses. A lunar eclipse is safe to watch with bare eyes.

example.q: Why can a solar eclipse happen only on a new moon day?
steps: In a solar eclipse the Moon must be between the Sun and the Earth.
The Moon is between the Sun and the Earth only around new moon.
So the Moon's shadow can fall on the Earth only then.
example.answer: Because only at new moon is the Moon between the Sun and the Earth.

learn.reallife: Scientists in India travel to places in the path of a total solar eclipse to study the Sun's outer layer, which is visible only when the Moon blocks the bright disc.

quiz.q: During a solar eclipse, which body is in the middle?
quiz.explain: The Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth and blocks the Sun's light.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the order in solar and lunar eclipses

quiz.q: During a lunar eclipse, whose shadow falls on the Moon?
quiz.explain: The Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon, so the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Moon is covered by the Sun

quiz.q: On which day can a lunar eclipse happen?
quiz.explain: Only at full moon is the Earth between the Sun and the Moon.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the moon phases for the two eclipses

quiz.q: Why don't we have a solar eclipse every new moon?
options: The Sun is too far away
The Moon's path is slightly tilted, so they usually do not line up exactly
quiz.explain: Most months the Moon passes a little above or below the line joining the Sun and the Earth.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the three bodies line up every month

quiz.q: What is the safe way to watch a solar eclipse?
options: Look through a camera without a filter
quiz.explain: Ordinary sunglasses are not safe. Only proper solar filters protect the eyes.
quiz.mistake: Thinks sunglasses are enough

quiz.q: Is it safe to watch a lunar eclipse with bare eyes?
options: No, it will harm your eyes
quiz.explain: The Moon's light is just reflected sunlight and is gentle on the eyes, so a lunar eclipse can be watched safely.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all eclipses are dangerous to look at

quiz.q: During a total lunar eclipse, how does the Moon often look?
quiz.explain: A little sunlight bends through the Earth's air and reaches the Moon, giving it a reddish glow.
quiz.mistake: Expects the Moon to vanish completely

quiz.q: In a solar eclipse, whose shadow falls on the Earth?
quiz.explain: The Moon blocks sunlight, and its shadow falls on a part of the Earth.
quiz.mistake: Confuses which body casts the shadow

teach.ask: Gappu heard there will be an eclipse soon. What is an eclipse, and are solar and lunar eclipses the same?
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! Moon in the middle: solar eclipse. Earth in the middle: lunar eclipse. Gappu will watch safely!
teach.nudge: Which body is in the middle during a lunar eclipse?
